security_audit.summary: All 80 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, documented placeholders, environment-based SDK setup, and official reference links. The skill contains no command execution, credential-directory access, or embedded secret. One medium contextual issue remains: several examples print configuration values, which may expose sensitive data through logs.

remediation.issue: Several examples print complete configuration values to standard output.
remediation.suggestion: Replace value-printing examples with keys, metadata, or redacted values, and warn users not to log configuration contents.

content.user_title: Build Java Apps with Azure App Configuration
content.value_statement: Java teams need consistent patterns for centralized settings and controlled releases. This skill provides focused Azure SDK guidance for configuration, feature flags, and snapshots.
actual_capabilities: Provides Maven dependency guidance for the Azure App Configuration Java client library.
Shows synchronous and asynchronous client creation with connection strings or Entra ID credentials.
Explains create, read, update, delete, conditional, and filtered setting operations.
Covers feature flags, Key Vault secret references, labels, and read-only settings.
Demonstrates snapshot creation, listing, archiving, recovery, and release-oriented filtering.
Includes ETag concurrency, reactive listing, and HTTP error-handling patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples but does not connect to Azure or modify resources automatically.
The examples require valid Azure permissions, endpoints, dependencies, and environment-specific testing.
The documented package version may not reflect the latest Azure SDK release.
It focuses on the low-level Java client and does not cover every Spring integration.

use_cases.title: Centralize Java Application Settings
use_cases.description: Create a labeled configuration workflow for development, staging, and production environments.

use_cases.title: Secure Cloud Configuration Access
use_cases.description: Configure Entra ID authentication and Key Vault references without embedding credentials in source code.

use_cases.title: Control Release Configuration
use_cases.description: Use feature flags, ETags, read-only settings, and snapshots for predictable deployments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up an Azure App Configuration client for my Java Maven project. Use Entra ID and an endpoint environment variable.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Labeled Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a Java workflow to create, read, update, and delete settings under the label [LABEL]. Include ETag protection.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Feature Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a percentage-based feature rollout for [FEATURE]. Include a Key Vault reference and safe rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Snapshot Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced Java design for release snapshots matching [KEY_FILTER]. Include async reads, concurrency handling, archival, recovery, and redacted logging.

output_examples.input: Set up secure access for a Java service using the production store.
output: Recommended Entra ID authentication with the store endpoint supplied through an environment variable.
Identified the required Azure role and Maven dependencies.
Added validation steps for local credentials and production managed identity.

output_examples.input: Plan a gradual rollout for the new checkout feature.
output: Defined a labeled feature flag with percentage targeting.
Included ETag checks to prevent conflicting updates.
Added disable, rollback, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Create a repeatable configuration release process.
output: Selected application keys with an environment label.
Created an immutable release snapshot and verification checklist.
Documented archive and recovery actions without printing setting values.

best_practices: Prefer Entra ID and managed identity over connection strings.
Use labels, ETags, and snapshots to separate environments and protect concurrent changes.
Keep secrets in Key Vault references and redact configuration values from logs.
anti_patterns: Do not embed connection strings, credentials, or secret values in source code.
Do not overwrite production settings without labels, ETag checks, or release validation.
Do not print complete configuration values during listing, troubleshooting, or reactive processing.

faq.question: Does this skill access my Azure account?
faq.answer: No. It provides Java guidance and examples. You must supply credentials, permissions, and endpoints in your environment.

faq.question: Which authentication method should I use?
faq.answer: Use Entra ID with managed identity when possible. Connection strings are supported but require stronger secret handling.

faq.question: Can it manage feature flags?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers creating, reading, updating, and percentage-targeting feature flag configuration settings.

faq.question: Does it support asynchronous applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes asynchronous client creation and reactive setting-list operations.

faq.question: How does it protect concurrent updates?
faq.answer: It demonstrates conditional requests with ETags so updates and deletes can require an unchanged setting.

faq.question: Does it retrieve secrets from Key Vault?
faq.answer: No. It creates and reads secret reference settings. Your application still needs Key Vault access and secret-resolution logic.
